chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from one of his companions, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
From the happiness of the man is that he removes the veil from a white woman.

key_terms.بَيْضَاءَ: White (often implying purity, beauty, or brightness)

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam say constitutes a man's happiness in marriage?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) links marital bliss (sa'adah) to the physical intimacy of unveiling one's spouse, using the term 'white' (bayda') to signify both physical beauty and spiritual purity. In Shia exegetical tradition, this brevity reflects the practical guidance for conjugal life, emphasizing that the removal of outer garments symbolizes the transition from public modesty to private intimacy, thereby fostering emotional and physical closeness between spouses.
